title: A watercolor sky
caption: Airglow and the Milky Way over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope stand guard beneath a star-filled sky in this view of Paranal Observatory. The glittering arch of our galaxy spans the scene, the glowing Magellanic Clouds sit on the left, and soft swathes of green, yellow, red and orange lie close to the horizon.

Chile's Atacama Desert is one of the darkest, quietest astronomical sites on Earth, which is why ESO has built its observatories there. Even so, Paranal's sky is not completely dark. After sunset, Earth's own atmosphere glows in many hues, painting the sky like a watercolor.

That colorful wash is airglow, a faint light produced by chemical processes up to a few hundred kilometers above the ground. It joins the distant emission nebulae dotting the Milky Way and the constellation of Orion in the upper center. At lower center, a diffuse white ray is sunlight reflecting off specks of rock and ice between the Sun and us.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at Paranal. The source gives no camera or exposure details.
understand.eye: The camera brings out the colors of the airglow and the Milky Way more strongly than the eye would see them.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The Sun had only just set in the west, at the center of the frame, when the picture was taken, which is why its light still catches those specks of rock and ice.
alt: VLT telescopes under an arching Milky Way, with the Magellanic Clouds on the left and bands of green, yellow, red and orange airglow near the horizon.
